Statement III: In neutral or faintly alkaline medium, permanganate ion oxidises thiosulphate ion (\(\mathrm{S}_2\mathrm{O}_3^{2-}\)) almost quantitatively to sulphate ion (\(\mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}\)).

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

क्रोमियम और मैंगनीज के ऑक्सोऋणायनों के संदर्भ में नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: डाइक्रोमेट आयन (\(\mathrm{Cr}_2\mathrm{O}_7^{2-}\)) में दो चतुष्फलकीय इकाइयाँ \(126^\circ\) के \(\mathrm{Cr-O-Cr}\) आबंध कोण पर एक ऑक्सीजन परमाणु साझा करती हैं।

कथन II: अम्लीय माध्यम में पोटैशियम परमैंगनेट ऑक्सैलेट आयन (\(\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{O}_4^{2-}\)) को कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड में ऑक्सीकृत करता है, जिसमें \(\mathrm{MnO}_4^-\) के दो मोल \(\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{O}_4^{2-}\) के पाँच मोल तथा \(\mathrm{H}^+\) के 16 मोल के साथ अभिक्रिया करते हैं।

कथन III: उदासीन या दुर्बल क्षारीय माध्यम में परमैंगनेट आयन थायोसल्फेट आयन (\(\mathrm{S}_2\mathrm{O}_3^{2-}\)) को लगभग मात्रात्मक रूप से सल्फेट आयन (\(\mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}\)) में ऑक्सीकृत करता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Structural and Redox Principles of Oxoanions
Transition metals in high oxidation states form stable oxoanions like dichromate (\(\mathrm{Cr}_2\mathrm{O}_7^{2-}\)) and permanganate (\(\mathrm{MnO}_4^-\)). Their structural geometries and stoichiometry in redox reactions are governed by electron-transfer balance and solution pH.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Statement
The dichromate ion consists of two tetrahedral \(\mathrm{CrO}_4\) units joined through a bridging oxygen atom at a shared vertex. The bridging \(\mathrm{Cr-O-Cr}\) bond angle is experimentally determined to be \(126^\circ\), with six terminal \(\mathrm{Cr-O}\) bonds possessing equivalent partial double-bond character. Hence, the first statement is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Statement
In acidic solution, permanganate undergoes a five-electron reduction: \(\mathrm{MnO}_4^- + 8\mathrm{H}^+ + 5e^- \rightarrow \mathrm{Mn}^{2+} + 4\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\). Oxalate undergoes a two-electron oxidation: \(\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{O}_4^{2-} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CO}_2 + 2e^-\). Multiplying the reduction half-reaction by 2 and the oxidation half-reaction by 5 yields the balanced overall equation: \(2\mathrm{MnO}_4^- + 5\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{O}_4^{2-} + 16\mathrm{H}^+ \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Mn}^{2+} + 10\mathrm{CO}_2 + 8\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\). Thus, two moles of permanganate react with five moles of oxalate and 16 moles of protons. Hence, the second statement is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Third Statement
In neutral or faintly alkaline medium, permanganate is reduced to manganese dioxide (\(\mathrm{MnO}_2\)) via a three-electron transfer. It oxidises thiosulphate quantitatively to sulphate according to the balanced reaction: \(8\mathrm{MnO}_4^- + 3\mathrm{S}_2\mathrm{O}_3^{2-} + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \rightarrow 8\mathrm{MnO}_2 + 6\mathrm{SO}_4^{2-} + 2\mathrm{OH}^-\). Hence, the third statement is correct.

Step 5: Final Conceptual Answer
All three statements are correct.

चरण 1: ऑक्सोऋणायनों की संरचना और रेडॉक्स सिद्धांत
उच्च ऑक्सीकरण अवस्थाओं में संक्रमण धातुएँ डाइक्रोमेट (\(\mathrm{Cr}_2\mathrm{O}_7^{2-}\)) और परमैंगनेट (\(\mathrm{MnO}_4^-\)) जैसे स्थायी ऑक्सोऋणायन बनाती हैं। रेडॉक्स अभिक्रियाओं में इनकी ज्यामिति और रससमीकरणमिति इलेक्ट्रॉन-स्थानांतरण संतुलन एवं विलयन के pH द्वारा नियंत्रित होती है।

चरण 2: प्रथम कथन का मूल्यांकन
डाइक्रोमेट आयन में दो चतुष्फलकीय \(\mathrm{CrO}_4\) इकाइयाँ एक साझा शीर्ष पर उपस्थित सेतु ऑक्सीजन परमाणु के माध्यम से जुड़ी होती हैं। प्रायोगिक रूप से सेतु \(\mathrm{Cr-O-Cr}\) आबंध कोण का मान \(126^\circ\) पाया जाता है, जबकि छह सीमांत \(\mathrm{Cr-O}\) आबंध समतुल्य आंशिक द्वि-आबंध लक्षण प्रदर्शित करते हैं। अतः प्रथम कथन सही है।

चरण 3: द्वितीय कथन का मूल्यांकन
अम्लीय विलयन में परमैंगनेट पाँच इलेक्ट्रॉनों का अपचयन दर्शाता है: \(\mathrm{MnO}_4^- + 8\mathrm{H}^+ + 5e^- \rightarrow \mathrm{Mn}^{2+} + 4\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)। ऑक्सैलेट दो इलेक्ट्रॉनों का ऑक्सीकरण दर्शाता है: \(\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{O}_4^{2-} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CO}_2 + 2e^-\)। अपचयन अर्ध-अभिक्रिया को 2 से तथा ऑक्सीकरण अर्ध-अभिक्रिया को 5 से गुणा करके जोड़ने पर संतुलित समीकरण प्राप्त होता है: \(2\mathrm{MnO}_4^- + 5\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{O}_4^{2-} + 16\mathrm{H}^+ \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Mn}^{2+} + 10\mathrm{CO}_2 + 8\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)। इस प्रकार, दो मोल परमैंगनेट पाँच मोल ऑक्सैलेट और 16 मोल प्रोटॉन के साथ अभिक्रिया करते हैं। अतः द्वितीय कथन सही है।

चरण 4: तृतीय कथन का मूल्यांकन
उदासीन अथवा दुर्बल क्षारीय माध्यम में परमैंगनेट तीन-इलेक्ट्रॉन स्थानांतरण के माध्यम से मैंगनीज डाइऑक्साइड (\(\mathrm{MnO}_2\)) में अपचयित होता है। यह थायोसल्फेट को संतुलित अभिक्रिया के अनुसार मात्रात्मक रूप से सल्फेट में ऑक्सीकृत करता है: \(8\mathrm{MnO}_4^- + 3\mathrm{S}_2\mathrm{O}_3^{2-} + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \rightarrow 8\mathrm{MnO}_2 + 6\mathrm{SO}_4^{2-} + 2\mathrm{OH}^-\)। अतः तृतीय कथन सही है।

चरण 5: अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर
तीनों कथन सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CLASS12_CHAPTER08_STATEMENT4_Q01 - Melting points oxidation states and magnetism in 3d series

questiontext.text:
Given below are four statements regarding the properties and electronic trends of 3d transition elements:

Statement I: Transition metals generally display high melting points due to the involvement of electrons from both \((n-1)d\) and \(ns\) orbitals in interatomic metallic bonding.

Statement II: Across the 3d transition series, scandium (\(Z = 21\)) does not exhibit variable oxidation states in its stable compounds and forms only the \(+3\) oxidation state.

Statement III: The \(\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}\) ion in aqueous solution exhibits a calculated spin-only magnetic moment of \(1.73\text{ BM}\).

Statement IV: The highest oxidation state of manganese is exhibited in its oxide \(\mathrm{Mn}_2\mathrm{O}_7\) (\(+7\)) rather than in its fluoride \(\mathrm{MnF}_4\) (\(+4\)) due to the ability of oxygen to form multiple bonds with the metal.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

3d संक्रमण तत्वों के गुणों और इलेक्ट्रॉनिक प्रवृत्तियों के संदर्भ में नीचे चार कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: अंतरापरमाणुक धात्विक आबंधन में \((n-1)d\) और \(ns\) दोनों कक्षकों के इलेक्ट्रॉनों के भाग लेने के कारण संक्रमण धातुएँ सामान्यतः उच्च गलनांक प्रदर्शित करती हैं।

कथन II: 3d संक्रमण श्रेणी में, स्कैंडियम (\(Z = 21\)) अपने स्थायी यौगिकों में परिवर्तनशील ऑक्सीकरण अवस्थाएँ प्रदर्शित नहीं करता है तथा केवल \(+3\) ऑक्सीकरण अवस्था बनाता है।

कथन III: जलीय विलयन में \(\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}\) आयन \(1.73\text{ BM}\) का परिकलित केवल-प्रचक्रण चुंबकीय आघूर्ण प्रदर्शित करता है।

कथन IV: धातु के साथ बहु-आबंध बनाने की ऑक्सीजन की क्षमता के कारण मैंगनीज की उच्चतम ऑक्सीकरण अवस्था इसके फ्लोराइड \(\mathrm{MnF}_4\) (\(+4\)) की तुलना में इसके ऑक्साइड \(\mathrm{Mn}_2\mathrm{O}_7\) (\(+7\)) में प्रदर्शित होती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principles of 3d Transition Element Characteristics
Transition metals are distinguished by metallic bonding involving penultimate \(d\) and outer \(s\) electrons, variable oxidation states from incomplete \(d\) subshells, magnetic moments governed by unpaired electrons, and stabilisation of high oxidation states by electronegative ligands.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Statement
The high melting points of transition metals are directly attributed to the participation of greater numbers of valence electrons from \((n-1)d\) in addition to outer \(ns\) electrons in delocalised metallic bonding. Hence, the first statement is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Statement
Scandium has atomic number \(Z = 21\) with the valence electronic configuration \(3d^1 4s^2\). By losing all three valence electrons, it achieves the noble-gas configuration of argon (\([\mathrm{Ar}] 3d^0\)). It does not possess any further electrons to exhibit higher states, nor can it stabilise intermediate lower states in stable compounds. Thus, scandium does not exhibit variable oxidation states and forms exclusively \(+3\) compounds. Hence, the second statement is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Third Statement
Zinc (\(Z = 30\)) has the valence configuration \(3d^{10} 4s^2\). When it forms the divalent ion \(\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}\), it loses the two \(4s\) electrons, leaving a completely filled \(3d^{10}\) subshell. The number of unpaired electrons is \(n = 0\), and its spin-only magnetic moment is \(\mu = \sqrt{0(0+2)} = 0\text{ BM}\). The value of \(1.73\text{ BM}\) corresponds to a species with one unpaired electron (\(n = 1\)). Hence, the third statement is incorrect.

Step 5: Evaluation of the Fourth Statement
Oxygen has the unique capability to form multiple covalent bonds (\(p\pi\text{–}d\pi\)) with transition metal atoms, allowing manganese to reach its maximum group oxidation state of \(+7\) in covalent \(\mathrm{Mn}_2\mathrm{O}_7\). In contrast, fluorine can only form single bonds, and steric crowding prevents more than four fluorine atoms from coordinating around manganese in simple halides, restricting the highest fluoride to \(\mathrm{MnF}_4\). Hence, the fourth statement is correct.

Step 6: Final Conceptual Answer
Only the first, second, and fourth statements are correct.

चरण 1: 3d संक्रमण तत्वों के गुणों का सिद्धांत
संक्रमण धातुएँ उपांत्य \(d\) और बाह्य \(s\) इलेक्ट्रॉनों द्वारा निर्मित धात्विक आबंधन, अपूर्ण \(d\) उपकोशों से उत्पन्न परिवर्तनशील ऑक्सीकरण अवस्थाओं, अयुग्मित इलेक्ट्रॉनों द्वारा निर्धारित चुंबकीय आघूर्णों तथा विद्युतऋणात्मक लिगेंडों द्वारा उच्च ऑक्सीकरण अवस्थाओं के स्थिरीकरण द्वारा पहचानी जाती हैं।

चरण 2: प्रथम कथन का मूल्यांकन
संक्रमण धातुओं के उच्च गलनांक अंतरापरमाणुक धात्विक आबंधन में बाह्य \(ns\) इलेक्ट्रॉनों के अतिरिक्त उपांत्य \((n-1)d\) कक्षकों के अधिक इलेक्ट्रॉनों के भाग लेने के कारण होते हैं। अतः प्रथम कथन सही है।

चरण 3: द्वितीय कथन का मूल्यांकन
स्कैंडियम का परमाणु क्रमांक \(Z = 21\) है जिसका संयोजी इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास \(3d^1 4s^2\) होता है। अपने तीनों संयोजी इलेक्ट्रॉनों को त्यागकर यह ऑर्गन का उत्कृष्ट गैस विन्यास (\([\mathrm{Ar}] 3d^0\)) प्राप्त करता है। इसके पास उच्च अवस्थाएँ दर्शाने के लिए कोई अतिरिक्त इलेक्ट्रॉन नहीं होते, और न ही यह स्थायी यौगिकों में मध्यवर्ती निम्न अवस्थाओं को स्थिर कर पाता है। अतः स्कैंडियम परिवर्तनशील ऑक्सीकरण अवस्थाएँ प्रदर्शित नहीं करता तथा केवल \(+3\) अवस्था बनाता है। अतः द्वितीय कथन सही है।

चरण 4: तृतीय कथन का मूल्यांकन
जिंक (\(Z = 30\)) का विन्यास \(3d^{10} 4s^2\) होता है। द्विधनात्मक आयन \(\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}\) के निर्माण में दो \(4s\) इलेक्ट्रॉन निकल जाते हैं, जिससे पूर्णतः भरा हुआ \(3d^{10}\) उपकोश शेष रहता है। अयुग्मित इलेक्ट्रॉनों की संख्या \(n = 0\) होने के कारण इसका केवल-प्रचक्रण चुंबकीय आघूर्ण \(\mu = \sqrt{0(0+2)} = 0\text{ BM}\) होता है। \(1.73\text{ BM}\) मान एक अयुग्मित इलेक्ट्रॉन (\(n = 1\)) वाली स्पीशीज का होता है। अतः तृतीय कथन गलत है।

चरण 5: चतुर्थ कथन का मूल्यांकन
ऑक्सीजन धातु के साथ बहु-आबंध (\(p\pi\text{–}d\pi\)) बनाने की विशिष्ट क्षमता रखती है, जिससे मैंगनीज \(\mathrm{Mn}_2\mathrm{O}_7\) में अपनी अधिकतम समूह ऑक्सीकरण अवस्था \(+7\) प्राप्त कर लेता है। इसके विपरीत, फ्लोरीन केवल एकल आबंध बना सकता है तथा त्रिविमीय बाधा के कारण सरल हैलाइड में चार से अधिक फ्लोरीन परमाणु नहीं जुड़ पाते, जिससे उच्चतम फ्लोराइड \(\mathrm{MnF}_4\) तक सीमित रहता है। अतः चतुर्थ कथन सही है।

चरण 6: अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर
केवल प्रथम, द्वितीय और चतुर्थ कथन सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CLASS12_CHAPTER08_STATEMENT4_Q02 - Oxoanions lanthanoid contraction and actinoid oxidation states

questiontext.text:
Given below are four statements regarding oxoanions of transition metals and inner transition elements:

Statement I: The chromate ion (\(\mathrm{CrO}_4^{2-}\)) is tetrahedral, while the dichromate ion (\(\mathrm{Cr}_2\mathrm{O}_7^{2-}\)) consists of two tetrahedra sharing one corner with a \(\mathrm{Cr-O-Cr}\) bond angle of \(126^\circ\).

Statement II: In neutral or faintly alkaline solution, potassium permanganate oxidises iodide ion (\(\mathrm{I}^-\)) to free iodine (\(\mathrm{I}_2\)).

Statement III: The almost identical atomic radii of zirconium (\(160\text{ pm}\)) and hafnium (\(159\text{ pm}\)) are a direct consequence of the lanthanoid contraction.

Statement IV: Actinoids exhibit a wider range of oxidation states than lanthanoids because their \(5f\), \(6d\), and \(7s\) energy levels are of comparable energies.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

संक्रमण धातुओं के ऑक्सोऋणायनों और आंतरिक संक्रमण तत्वों के संदर्भ में नीचे चार कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: क्रोमेट आयन (\(\mathrm{CrO}_4^{2-}\)) चतुष्फलकीय होता है, जबकि डाइक्रोमेट आयन (\(\mathrm{Cr}_2\mathrm{O}_7^{2-}\)) में दो चतुष्फलकीय इकाइयाँ \(126^\circ\) के \(\mathrm{Cr-O-Cr}\) आबंध कोण पर एक कोना साझा करती हैं।

कथन II: उदासीन या दुर्बल क्षारीय विलयन में, पोटैशियम परमैंगनेट आयोडाइड आयन (\(\mathrm{I}^-\)) को मुक्त आयोडीन (\(\mathrm{I}_2\)) में ऑक्सीकृत करता है।

कथन III: ज़िरकोनियम (\(160\text{ pm}\)) और हाफ्नियम (\(159\text{ pm}\)) की लगभग समरूप परमाणु त्रिज्याएँ लैन्थेनॉइड आकुंचन का प्रत्यक्ष परिणाम हैं।

कथन IV: ऐक्टिनॉइड, लैन्थेनॉइडों की तुलना में ऑक्सीकरण अवस्थाओं का एक विस्तृत परास प्रदर्शित करते हैं क्योंकि उनके \(5f\), \(6d\) और \(7s\) ऊर्जा स्तरों की ऊर्जाएँ तुलनीय होती हैं।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Structural and Electronic Principles of Oxoanions and f-Block Elements
The structures of oxoanions depend on tetrahedral coordination of oxygen atoms around transition metals, their redox pathways depend heavily on medium pH, and the spatial distribution and energy levels of inner \(f\) orbitals govern lanthanoid and actinoid chemistry.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Statement
The yellow chromate ion (\(\mathrm{CrO}_4^{2-}\)) possesses a discrete tetrahedral geometry. In the orange dichromate ion (\(\mathrm{Cr}_2\mathrm{O}_7^{2-}\)), two tetrahedral \(\mathrm{CrO}_4\) units share a common oxygen vertex with an experimentally established bridging \(\mathrm{Cr-O-Cr}\) bond angle of \(126^\circ\). Hence, the first statement is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Statement
In acidic medium, permanganate oxidises iodide to elemental iodine: \(2\mathrm{MnO}_4^- + 10\mathrm{I}^- + 16\mathrm{H}^+ \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Mn}^{2+} + 5\mathrm{I}_2 + 8\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\). However, in neutral or faintly alkaline medium, permanganate undergoes a three-electron reduction to \(\mathrm{MnO}_2\) and oxidises iodide quantitatively to iodate (\(\mathrm{IO}_3^-\)), according to the equation: \(2\mathrm{MnO}_4^- + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} + \mathrm{I}^- \rightarrow 2\mathrm{MnO}_2 + 2\mathrm{OH}^- + \mathrm{IO}_3^-\). Claiming that it yields free iodine in neutral/faintly alkaline medium is false. Hence, the second statement is incorrect.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Third Statement
The intervention of the fourteen \(4f\) electrons prior to the \(5d\) elements results in poor shielding of the increasing nuclear charge, producing a continuous reduction in size known as the lanthanoid contraction. This contraction precisely compensates for the expected group increase from period 5 to period 6, causing zirconium (\(\mathrm{Zr} = 160\text{ pm}\)) and hafnium (\(\mathrm{Hf} = 159\text{ pm}\)) to have virtually identical atomic and ionic radii. Hence, the third statement is correct.

Step 5: Evaluation of the Fourth Statement
In actinoids, the \(5f\) orbitals extend further outward and are less deeply buried than the \(4f\) orbitals in lanthanoids. Because the energy difference between the \(5f\), \(6d\), and \(7s\) subshells is exceptionally small, electrons from all these levels can participate in bonding, leading to multiple stable oxidation states (from \(+3\) up to \(+7\)). Hence, the fourth statement is correct.

Step 6: Final Conceptual Answer
Only the first, third, and fourth statements are correct.

चरण 1: ऑक्सोऋणायनों और f-ब्लॉक तत्वों के संरचनात्मक व इलेक्ट्रॉनिक सिद्धांत
ऑक्सोऋणायनों की संरचनाएँ संक्रमण धातुओं के चारों ओर ऑक्सीजन परमाणुओं के चतुष्फलकीय विन्यास पर निर्भर करती हैं, इनके रेडॉक्स मार्ग माध्यम के pH पर निर्भर करते हैं, तथा आंतरिक \(f\) कक्षकों का स्थानिक प्रसार और ऊर्जा स्तर लैन्थेनॉइड व ऐक्टिनॉइड रसायन को नियंत्रित करते हैं।

चरण 2: प्रथम कथन का मूल्यांकन
पीले रंग का क्रोमेट आयन (\\(\\mathrm{CrO}_4^{2-}\\)) एक पृथक चतुष्फलकीय ज्यामिति रखता है। नारंगी डाइक्रोमेट आयन (\\(\\mathrm{Cr}_2\\mathrm{O}_7^{2-}\\)) में दो चतुष्फलकीय \\(\\mathrm{CrO}_4\\) इकाइयाँ एक उभयनिष्ठ ऑक्सीजन शीर्ष साझा करती हैं, जिसका प्रायोगिक रूप से निर्धारित सेतु \\(\\mathrm{Cr-O-Cr}\\) आबंध कोण \\(126^\\circ\\) होता है। अतः प्रथम कथन सही है।

चरण 3: द्वितीय कथन का मूल्यांकन
अम्लीय माध्यम में परमैंगनेट आयोडाइड को मुक्त आयोडीन में ऑक्सीकृत करता है: \\(2\\mathrm{MnO}_4^- + 10\\mathrm{I}^- + 16\\mathrm{H}^+ \\rightarrow 2\\mathrm{Mn}^{2+} + 5\\mathrm{I}_2 + 8\\mathrm{H}_2\\mathrm{O}\\)। परंतु उदासीन या दुर्बल क्षारीय माध्यम में परमैंगनेट तीन-इलेक्ट्रॉन अपचयन द्वारा \\(\\mathrm{MnO}_2\\) में परिवर्तित होता है तथा आयोडाइड को आयोडेट (\\(\\mathrm{IO}_3^-\\)) में मात्रात्मक रूप से ऑक्सीकृत करता है: \\(2\\mathrm{MnO}_4^- + \\mathrm{H}_2\\mathrm{O} + \\mathrm{I}^- \\rightarrow 2\\mathrm{MnO}_2 + 2\\mathrm{OH}^- + \\mathrm{IO}_3^-\\)। यह कहना कि यह उदासीन/क्षारीय माध्यम में मुक्त आयोडीन देता है, असत्य है। अतः द्वितीय कथन गलत है।

चरण 4: तृतीय कथन का मूल्यांकन
\\(5d\\) श्रेणी से पूर्व चौदह \\(4f\\) इलेक्ट्रॉनों का भरा जाना बढ़ते नाभिकीय आवेश का दुर्बल परिरक्षण करता है, जिससे आकारों में नियमित कमी आती है जिसे लैन्थेनॉइड आकुंचन कहते हैं। यह आकुंचन आवर्त 5 से आवर्त 6 तक अपेक्षित आकार वृद्धि को पूर्णतः संतुलित कर देता है, जिससे ज़िरकोनियम (\\(\\mathrm{Zr} = 160\\text{ pm}\\)) और हाफ्नियम (\\(\\mathrm{Hf} = 159\\text{ pm}\\)) की परमाणु और आयनिक त्रिज्याएँ लगभग समरूप होती हैं। अतः तृतीय कथन सही है।

चरण 5: चतुर्थ कथन का मूल्यांकन
ऐक्टिनॉइडों में \\(5f\\) कक्षक लैन्थेनॉइडों के \\(4f\\) कक्षकों की तुलना में अधिक बाहर तक विस्तृत होते हैं। चूँकि \\(5f\\), \\(6d\\) और \\(7s\\) उपकोशों के मध्य ऊर्जा अंतर अत्यधिक कम होता है, अतः इन सभी स्तरों के इलेक्ट्रॉन आबंधन में भाग ले सकते हैं, जिससे ऐक्टिनॉइड कई ऑक्सीकरण अवस्थाएँ (\\(+3\\) से लेकर \\(+7\\) तक) प्रदर्शित करते हैं। अतः चतुर्थ कथन सही है।

चरण 6: अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर
केवल प्रथम, तृतीय और चतुर्थ कथन सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q01 - Industrial catalysts and their chemical processes

questiontext.text:
Match the catalyst listed in List I with the corresponding industrial process or reaction in List II:

List I (Catalyst) List II (Process / Reaction)
(A) \(\text{V}_2\text{O}_5\) (I) Manufacture of ammonia
(B) Finely divided \(\text{Fe}\) (II) Oxidation of ethyne to ethanal (Wacker process)
(C) \(\text{PdCl}_2\) (III) Manufacture of sulphuric acid (Contact process)
(D) \(\text{TiCl}_4\) with \(\text{Al(CH}_3)_3\) (IV) Manufacture of polyethylene

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Transition metals and their compounds exhibit notable catalytic activity due to their variable oxidation states, ability to form complexes, and provision of suitable reaction pathways by adsorption and bond weakening.

Step 2: Evaluation of individual catalytic applications
- Vanadium(V) oxide (\(\text{V}_2\text{O}_5\)) catalyses the oxidation of \(\text{SO}_2\) to \(\text{SO}_3\) in the Contact process during the manufacture of sulphuric acid.
- Finely divided iron (\(\text{Fe}\)) is used as the heterogeneous catalyst in the Haber process for the synthesis of ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen.
- Palladium(II) chloride (\(\text{PdCl}_2\)) serves as the catalyst in the Wacker process for the oxidation of ethyne to ethanal.
- Titanium tetrachloride with trimethylaluminium (\(\text{TiCl}_4 + \text{Al(CH}_3)_3\)) forms the Ziegler–Natta catalyst utilized in the coordination polymerisation of ethene to manufacture polyethylene.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Pairing each catalyst with its process results in: \(\text{V}_2\text{O}_5\) with the manufacture of sulphuric acid (Contact process), finely divided \(\text{Fe}\) with the manufacture of ammonia, \(\text{PdCl}_2\) with the oxidation of ethyne to ethanal (Wacker process), and \(\text{TiCl}_4 + \text{Al(CH}_3)_3\) with the manufacture of polyethylene. Hence, the correct correspondence is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(IV).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q02 - Aqueous colors of first row transition ions

questiontext.text:
Match the hydrated transition metal ion in List I with its characteristic aqueous solution color in List II:

List I (Aqueous Ion) List II (Observed Color)
(A) \(\text{Ti}^{3+}\) (I) Yellow
(B) \(\text{Fe}^{3+}\) (II) Purple
(C) \(\text{Ni}^{2+}\) (III) Pink
(D) \(\text{Mn}^{2+}\) (IV) Green

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The color of aquated transition metal ions arises from \(d\text{–}d\) electronic transitions wherein an electron from a lower energy \(d\) orbital absorbs visible light to promote to a higher energy \(d\) orbital. The complementary color of the absorbed radiation is transmitted and perceived.

Step 2: Identification of individual ion colors
- Titanium(III) ion (\(\text{Ti}^{3+}\), configuration \(3d^1\)) exhibits a characteristic purple color.
- Iron(III) ion (\(\text{Fe}^{3+}\), configuration \(3d^5\)) produces a yellow solution in aqueous medium.
- Nickel(II) ion (\(\text{Ni}^{2+}\), configuration \(3d^8\)) exhibits a distinctive green color.
- Manganese(II) ion (\(\text{Mn}^{2+}\), configuration \(3d^5\)) displays a characteristic pale pink color.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Correlating each ion to its color gives: \(\text{Ti}^{3+}\) matches purple, \(\text{Fe}^{3+}\) matches yellow, \(\text{Ni}^{2+}\) matches green, and \(\text{Mn}^{2+}\) matches pink. This establishes the set (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q03 - Spin only magnetic moments of divalent ions

questiontext.text:
Match the divalent gaseous/aqueous transition metal ion in List I with its calculated spin-only magnetic moment in List II:

List I (Divalent Ion) List II (Magnetic Moment, \(\mu\) / BM)
(A) \(\text{V}^{2+}\) (I) \(4.90\text{ BM}\)
(B) \(\text{Mn}^{2+}\) (II) \(2.84\text{ BM}\)
(C) \(\text{Fe}^{2+}\) (III) \(3.87\text{ BM}\)
(D) \(\text{Ni}^{2+}\) (IV) \(5.92\text{ BM}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Formula and Principle
The spin-only magnetic moment is calculated using the relation: \[\mu = \sqrt{n(n + 2)}\text{ BM}\] where \(n\) is the number of unpaired \(d\)-electrons.

Step 2: Electronic configuration and unpaired electron count
- Vanadium (\(Z = 23\)): Neutral atom is \([\text{Ar}]\,3d^3\,4s^2\). For \(\text{V}^{2+}\), the outer configuration is \(3d^3\). The number of unpaired electrons is \(n = 3\). \[\mu = \sqrt{3(3 + 2)} = \sqrt{15} \approx 3.87\text{ BM}\] - Manganese (\(Z = 25\)): Neutral atom is \([\text{Ar}]\,3d^5\,4s^2\). For \(\text{Mn}^{2+}\), the outer configuration is \(3d^5\). The number of unpaired electrons is \(n = 5\). \[\mu = \sqrt{5(5 + 2)} = \sqrt{35} \approx 5.92\text{ BM}\] - Iron (\(Z = 26\)): Neutral atom is \([\text{Ar}]\,3d^6\,4s^2\). For \(\text{Fe}^{2+}\), the outer configuration is \(3d^6\). The number of unpaired electrons is \(n = 10 - 6 = 4\). \[\mu = \sqrt{4(4 + 2)} = \sqrt{24} \approx 4.90\text{ BM}\] - Nickel (\(Z = 28\)): Neutral atom is \([\text{Ar}]\,3d^8\,4s^2\). For \(\text{Ni}^{2+}\), the outer configuration is \(3d^8\). The number of unpaired electrons is \(n = 10 - 8 = 2\). \[\mu = \sqrt{2(2 + 2)} = \sqrt{8} \approx 2.84\text{ BM}\]

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Matching the calculated values yields: \(\text{V}^{2+}\) corresponds to \(3.87\text{ BM}\), \(\text{Mn}^{2+}\) corresponds to \(5.92\text{ BM}\), \(\text{Fe}^{2+}\) corresponds to \(4.90\text{ BM}\), and \(\text{Ni}^{2+}\) corresponds to \(2.84\text{ BM}\). Thus, the correct sequence is (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q04 - Highest oxides and oxocations oxidation states

questiontext.text:
Match the transition metal oxide or oxocation in List I with the oxidation state of the central transition metal in List II:

List I (Species) List II (Oxidation State)
(A) \(\text{Mn}_2\text{O}_7\) (I) \(+4\)
(B) \(\text{CrO}_3\) (II) \(+5\)
(C) \(\text{VO}_2^+\) (III) \(+6\)
(D) \(\text{TiO}^{2+}\) (IV) \(+7\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Relevant Principles
The oxidation state of the transition metal is determined from the neutral molecule or net cationic charge by assigning each oxo ligand an oxidation state of \(-2\).

Step 2: Evaluation of individual species
- For \(\text{Mn}_2\text{O}_7\): Let the oxidation state of \(\text{Mn}\) be \(x\). \[2x + 7(-2) = 0 \implies 2x = 14 \implies x = +7\] - For \(\text{CrO}_3\): Let the oxidation state of \(\text{Cr}\) be \(x\). \[x + 3(-2) = 0 \implies x = +6\] - For dioxovanadium(V) cation \(\text{VO}_2^+\): Let the oxidation state of \(\text{V}\) be \(x\). \[x + 2(-2) = +1 \implies x - 4 = +1 \implies x = +5\] - For oxotitanium(IV) cation \(\text{TiO}^{2+}\): Let the oxidation state of \(\text{Ti}\) be \(x\). \[x + 1(-2) = +2 \implies x = +4\]

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Matching each species to the deduced oxidation state yields: \(\text{Mn}_2\text{O}_7\) corresponds to \(+7\), \(\text{CrO}_3\) corresponds to \(+6\), \(\text{VO}_2^+\) corresponds to \(+5\), and \(\text{TiO}^{2+}\) corresponds to \(+4\). This establishes the set (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q05 - Permanganate oxidations in neutral and acidic media

questiontext.text:
Match the reactant being oxidised by potassium permanganate (\(\text{KMnO}_4\)) in List I with the principal oxidized product formed in List II:

List I (Reactant and Medium) List II (Oxidized Product)
(A) \(\text{I}^-\) in neutral or faintly alkaline medium (I) \(\text{SO}_4^{2-}\)
(B) \(\text{I}^-\) in acidic medium (II) \(\text{CO}_2\)
(C) \(\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}\) in neutral or faintly alkaline medium (III) \(\text{IO}_3^-\)
(D) \(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}\) in acidic medium at \(333\text{ K}\) (IV) \(\text{I}_2\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Chemical reactions of permanganate
Potassium permanganate acts as a strong oxidant whose reduction pathway and resulting oxidized products depend strictly on the pH of the medium.

Step 2: Evaluation of each specific transformation
- Oxidation of iodide in neutral/faintly alkaline medium: Iodide is quantitatively oxidized to iodate: \[2\text{MnO}_4^- + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{I}^- \rightarrow 2\text{MnO}_2 + 2\text{OH}^- + \text{IO}_3^-\] - Oxidation of iodide in acidic medium: Iodide is oxidized to elemental iodine: \[2\text{MnO}_4^- + 16\text{H}^+ + 10\text{I}^- \rightarrow 2\text{Mn}^{2+} + 8\text{H}_2\text{O} + 5\text{I}_2\] - Oxidation of thiosulphate in neutral/faintly alkaline medium: Thiosulphate is oxidized almost quantitatively to sulphate: \[8\text{MnO}_4^- + 3\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 8\text{MnO}_2 + 6\text{SO}_4^{2-} + 2\text{OH}^-\] - Oxidation of oxalate in acidic medium at \(333\text{ K}\): Oxalate is oxidized to carbon dioxide: \[2\text{MnO}_4^- + 16\text{H}^+ + 5\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} \rightarrow 2\text{Mn}^{2+} + 8\text{H}_2\text{O} + 10\text{CO}_2\]

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Pairing each reactant and condition with its primary product yields: \(\text{I}^-\) in neutral medium gives \(\text{IO}_3^-\), \(\text{I}^-\) in acidic medium gives \(\text{I}_2\), \(\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}\) in neutral medium gives \(\text{SO}_4^{2-}\), and \(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}\) in acidic medium gives \(\text{CO}_2\). This corresponds to (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q06 - Chemical reactions of lanthanoid metals

questiontext.text:
Match the reagent reacting with a lanthanoid metal (\(\text{Ln}\)) in List I with the resulting chemical product in List II:

List I (Reagent / Condition) List II (Product Formula)
(A) Heated with Nitrogen (\(\text{N}_2\)) (I) \(\text{LnC}_2\)
(B) Heated with Sulphur (\(\text{S}\)) (II) \(\text{LnN}\)
(C) Heated with Carbon (\(\text{C}\)) at \(2773\text{ K}\) (III) \(\text{Ln(OH)}_3 + \text{H}_2\)
(D) Reaction with water (\(\text{H}_2\text{O}\)) (IV) \(\text{Ln}_2\text{S}_3\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Chemical behavior of lanthanoids
Lanthanoids generally form compounds in their most stable oxidation state of \(+3\). Their standard reactivity resembles highly electropositive metals like calcium or aluminium.

Step 2: Evaluation of products
- Heating with nitrogen gas: Lanthanoids react directly with nitrogen to form mononitrides of composition \(\text{LnN}\).
- Heating with sulphur: Lanthanoids react with sulphur to yield sesquisulphides of composition \(\text{Ln}_2\text{S}_3\).
- Heating with carbon at elevated temperatures (\(2773\text{ K}\)): Lanthanoids combine with carbon to form dicarbides having the formula \(\text{LnC}_2\) (along with other stoichiometric carbides like \(\text{Ln}_3\text{C}\) and \(\text{Ln}_2\text{C}_3\)).
- Reaction with water: Lanthanoids react with water to form basic trihydroxides with liberation of hydrogen gas, following the stoichiometry \(\text{Ln(OH)}_3 + \text{H}_2\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Matching the reagents to products yields: heating with nitrogen gives \(\text{LnN}\), heating with sulphur gives \(\text{Ln}_2\text{S}_3\), heating with carbon gives \(\text{LnC}_2\), and reaction with water gives \(\text{Ln(OH)}_3 + \text{H}_2\). This corresponds to (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(III).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q07 - Electronic configurations of f block tripositive ions

questiontext.text:
Match the tripositive lanthanoid or actinoid ion in List I with its ground-state valence electronic configuration in List II:

List I (Tripositive Ion) List II (Valence Configuration)
(A) \(\text{Ce}^{3+}\) (\(Z = 58\)) (I) \(4f^7\)
(B) \(\text{Gd}^{3+}\) (\(Z = 64\)) (II) \(5f^7\)
(C) \(\text{Lu}^{3+}\) (\(Z = 71\)) (III) \(4f^1\)
(D) \(\text{Cm}^{3+}\) (\(Z = 96\)) (IV) \(4f^{14}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Principles of electronic configurations of \(f\)-block ions
In the formation of tripositive lanthanoid (\(\text{Ln}^{3+}\)) and actinoid (\(\text{An}^{3+}\)) ions, the outermost \(s\) electrons and any outer \(d\) electrons are removed first, leaving an \(f^n\) configuration.

Step 2: Configuration deduction
- Cerium (\(Z = 58\)): Ground-state neutral atom is \([\text{Xe}]\,4f^1\,5d^1\,6s^2\). Loss of three electrons (two from \(6s\) and one from \(5d\)) yields \(\text{Ce}^{3+}\) with the configuration \(4f^1\).
- Gadolinium (\(Z = 64\)): Ground-state neutral atom is \([\text{Xe}]\,4f^7\,5d^1\,6s^2\). Removal of three electrons leaves the half-filled stable core \([\text{Xe}]\,4f^7\).
- Lutetium (\(Z = 71\)): Ground-state neutral atom is \([\text{Xe}]\,4f^{14}\,5d^1\,6s^2\). Removal of three electrons leaves the completely filled stable core \([\text{Xe}]\,4f^{14}\).
- Curium (\(Z = 96\)): Ground-state neutral atom is \([\text{Rn}]\,5f^7\,6d^1\,7s^2\). Removal of three electrons gives \(\text{Cm}^{3+}\) with the half-filled configuration \(5f^7\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Matching each ion with its electronic configuration results in: \(\text{Ce}^{3+}\) pairs with \(4f^1\), \(\text{Gd}^{3+}\) pairs with \(4f^7\), \(\text{Lu}^{3+}\) pairs with \(4f^{14}\), and \(\text{Cm}^{3+}\) pairs with \(5f^7\). This corresponds to (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q08 - Standard electrode potentials of transition couples

questiontext.text:
Match the redox couple of the first row transition metals in List I with its corresponding standard electrode potential value (\(E^\circ\)) in List II:

List I (Redox Couple) List II (\(E^\circ / \text{V}\))
(A) \(\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu}\) (I) \(+1.57\text{ V}\)
(B) \(\text{Mn}^{3+}/\text{Mn}^{2+}\) (II) \(-0.41\text{ V}\)
(C) \(\text{Cr}^{3+}/\text{Cr}^{2+}\) (III) \(+0.77\text{ V}\)
(D) \(\text{Fe}^{3+}/\text{Fe}^{2+}\) (IV) \(+0.34\text{ V}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Basis of Electrode Potentials
Standard reduction potentials reflect the combined energetic terms of atomisation, successive ionisations, and ionic hydration. For \(M^{3+}/M^{2+}\), the potential depends primarily on the magnitude of the third ionisation enthalpy and the electronic stability of the resulting configurations.

Step 2: Evaluation of individual potential values
- \(\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu}\): Copper has a positive \(E^\circ\) of \(+0.34\text{ V}\) because the sum of its high enthalpy of atomisation and high ionisation enthalpies is not compensated by the hydration enthalpy of \(\text{Cu}^{2+}\).
- \(\text{Mn}^{3+}/\text{Mn}^{2+}\): Possesses an unusually high positive potential of \(+1.57\text{ V}\) because reduction converts the less stable \(d^4\) ion into the exceptionally stable half-filled \(d^5\) ion (\(\text{Mn}^{2+}\)), accompanied by a very high third ionisation enthalpy of manganese.
- \(\text{Cr}^{3+}/\text{Cr}^{2+}\): Has a negative potential of \(-0.41\text{ V}\) because \(\text{Cr}^{2+}\) (\(d^4\)) readily undergoes oxidation to \(\text{Cr}^{3+}\) which possesses a stable, half-filled \(t_{2g}^3\) sub-level.
- \(\text{Fe}^{3+}/\text{Fe}^{2+}\): Shows a moderately positive potential of \(+0.77\text{ V}\), where \(\text{Fe}^{3+}\) (\(d^5\)) has extra stability relative to \(\text{Fe}^{2+}\) (\(d^6\)).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Pairing each redox couple with its value gives: \(\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu}\) matches \(+0.34\text{ V}\), \(\text{Mn}^{3+}/\text{Mn}^{2+}\) matches \(+1.57\text{ V}\), \(\text{Cr}^{3+}/\text{Cr}^{2+}\) matches \(-0.41\text{ V}\), and \(\text{Fe}^{3+}/\text{Fe}^{2+}\) matches \(+0.77\text{ V}\). This corresponds to (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q09 - Structural and magnetic features of oxoanions

questiontext.text:
Match the oxoanion of transition metals in List I with its structural or magnetic characteristic in List II:

List I (Oxoanion) List II (Characteristic Feature)
(A) \(\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}\) (I) Tetrahedral geometry, green color, paramagnetic (\(1\) unpaired electron)
(B) \(\text{MnO}_4^{2-}\) (II) Tetrahedral geometry, intense purple color, diamagnetic
(C) \(\text{MnO}_4^-\) (III) Two tetrahedra sharing a corner with a bond angle of \(126^\circ\)
(D) \(\text{CrO}_4^{2-}\) (IV) Discrete tetrahedral geometry, yellow color, converts to dichromate in acid

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Structural and Electronic Principles
Chromate, dichromate, manganate, and permanganate are oxoanions where \(\pi\)-bonding arises from the overlap of \(p\)-orbitals of oxygen with \(d\)-orbitals of the transition metal.

Step 2: Analysis of individual oxoanions
- Dichromate ion (\(\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}\)): Consists of two tetrahedral units sharing a single oxygen corner, featuring bridging \(\text{Cr–O–Cr}\) bonds with an angle of \(126^\circ\).
- Manganate ion (\(\text{MnO}_4^{2-}\)): Possesses tetrahedral geometry with manganese in the \(+6\) oxidation state (\(3d^1\)). Because of the presence of one unpaired electron, it is paramagnetic and green in color.
- Permanganate ion (\(\text{MnO}_4^-\)): Possesses tetrahedral geometry with manganese in the \(+7\) oxidation state (\(3d^0\)). It lacks unpaired \(d\) electrons, making it diamagnetic, while exhibiting an intense purple color due to charge transfer.
- Chromate ion (\(\text{CrO}_4^{2-}\)): A discrete yellow tetrahedral species with chromium in the \(+6\) oxidation state; upon acidification, it undergoes condensation to form the orange dichromate ion.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Matching the oxoanions to their features yields: \(\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}\) matches two tetrahedra sharing one corner with a \(126^\circ\) angle, \(\text{MnO}_4^{2-}\) matches green and paramagnetic, \(\text{MnO}_4^-\) matches purple and diamagnetic, and \(\text{CrO}_4^{2-}\) matches discrete yellow tetrahedron converting to dichromate in acid. This corresponds to (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(IV).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q10 - Chemical rationale for transition element anomalies

questiontext.text:
Match the observed property/phenomenon of \(d\)- and \(f\)-block elements in List I with its primary underlying chemical cause in List II:

List I (Observed Phenomenon) List II (Primary Chemical Cause)
(A) Nearly identical atomic radii of \(\text{Zr}\) (\(160\text{ pm}\)) and \(\text{Hf}\) (\(159\text{ pm}\)) (I) Much more negative hydration enthalpy of the divalent ion overcompensating the second ionisation enthalpy
(B) Greater stability of \(\text{Cu}^{2+}\text{(aq)}\) relative to \(\text{Cu}^+\text{(aq)}\) (II) Intervention and poor shielding of completely filled \(4f\) subshell across the lanthanoids
(C) Abnormally low enthalpy of atomisation of Zinc (\(126\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\)) (III) Less penetration of \(5f\) orbitals and poorer shielding by \(5f\) electrons compared to \(4f\)
(D) Greater extent of actinoid contraction compared to lanthanoid contraction (IV) Absence of unpaired \(d\)-electrons resulting in no contribution of \(d\)-electrons to metallic bonding

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Underlying Principles
Specific chemical and physical trends across the \(d\)- and \(f\)-block elements are governed by shielding capabilities of diffuse inner subshells, exchange stabilization, and thermodynamic enthalpy balances.

Step 2: Evaluation of each correlation
- The similarity in atomic radii between \(\text{Zr}\) and \(\text{Hf}\) is a direct consequence of the lanthanoid contraction, which is caused by the poor shielding effect of the fourteen \(4f\) electrons filled prior to the \(5d\) series, compensating for the expected normal increase in atomic size with increasing atomic number.
- The higher stability and disproportionation of copper(I) into copper(II) in aqueous solution occurs because the enthalpy of hydration for \(\text{Cu}^{2+}\text{(aq)}\) is much more negative than that for \(\text{Cu}^+\text{(aq)}\), which more than compensates for the energy required for the second ionisation of copper.
- Zinc has the lowest enthalpy of atomisation (\(126\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\)) in the \(3d\) series because all its \(3d\) orbitals are completely filled (\(3d^{10}\)); hence, no unpaired \(d\) electrons participate in interatomic metallic bonding, leaving only weak metallic interactions involving \(4s\) electrons.
- Actinoid contraction is greater from element to element than lanthanoid contraction because \(5f\) orbitals penetrate less into the inner core, and \(5f\) electrons provide poorer shielding against the increasing nuclear charge than \(4f\) electrons.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Matching each phenomenon to its scientific cause gives: \(\text{Zr}/\text{Hf}\) radius similarity pairs with poor shielding of \(4f\) subshell (lanthanoid contraction), stability of aqueous \(\text{Cu}^{2+}\) pairs with the highly negative hydration enthalpy overcoming the second ionisation enthalpy, low atomisation enthalpy of zinc pairs with absence of unpaired \(d\) electrons in metallic bonding, and greater actinoid contraction pairs with poorer shielding of \(5f\) compared to \(4f\). This corresponds to (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_NUMERICAL_Q01 - Spin-only magnetic moment calculation for vanadium(III) ion

questiontext.text: What is the 'spin-only' magnetic moment of the aquated vanadium(III) ion, \(\text{V}^{3+}_{\text{(aq)}}\) (atomic number of vanadium, \(Z = 23\))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The central element is vanadium with atomic number \(Z = 23\). The ion has an oxidation state of \(+3\) (\(\text{V}^{3+}\)).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The ground-state electronic configuration of neutral vanadium is \([\text{Ar}]\,3d^34s^2\). During ionisation to \(\text{V}^{3+}\), the two \(4s\) electrons and one \(3d\) electron are lost, leaving the outer configuration \([\text{Ar}]\,3d^2\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
In first-row transition metal ions, orbital angular momentum is quenched by the ligand field. The 'spin-only' magnetic moment is given by \(\mu = \sqrt{n(n + 2)}\text{ BM}\), where \(n\) is the number of unpaired electrons.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
For the \(3d^2\) configuration, there are \(n = 2\) unpaired electrons. Substituting \(n = 2\) into the formula: \[\mu = \sqrt{2(2 + 2)} = \sqrt{8} \approx 2.84\text{ BM}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The calculated value of \(2.84\text{ BM}\) matches the theoretical spin-only magnetic moment for two unpaired electrons.

Therefore, the correct answer is: \(2.84\text{ BM}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_NUMERICAL_Q02 - Sum of unpaired d electrons in manganese(II) and iron(II) cations

questiontext.text: What is the total sum of the number of unpaired electrons present in the free gaseous divalent cations \(\text{Mn}^{2+}\) (\(Z = 25\)) and \(\text{Fe}^{2+}\) (\(Z = 26\)) in their ground states?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The two ions are \(\text{Mn}^{2+}\) (\(Z = 25\)) and \(\text{Fe}^{2+}\) (\(Z = 26\)) in their ground states.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Electrons fill degenerate \(3d\) orbitals following Hund's rule of maximum multiplicity to minimize electron-electron repulsion.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Neutral \(\text{Mn}\) has configuration \([\text{Ar}]\,3d^54s^2\), so \(\text{Mn}^{2+}\) has configuration \(3d^5\). Neutral \(\text{Fe}\) has configuration \([\text{Ar}]\,3d^64s^2\), so \(\text{Fe}^{2+}\) has configuration \(3d^6\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
In \(\text{Mn}^{2+}\) (\(3d^5\)), all five \(d\) electrons occupy separate orbitals with parallel spins, giving \(n_1 = 5\) unpaired electrons. In \(\text{Fe}^{2+}\) (\(3d^6\)), five electrons have parallel spins and one electron pairs up, giving \(n_2 = 4\) unpaired electrons. Total sum: \[n_{\text{total}} = 5 + 4 = 9\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Both configurations are high-spin ground states; \(5 + 4 = 9\) unpaired electrons.

Therefore, the correct answer is: \(9\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_NUMERICAL_Q03 - Mass calculation of lanthanoid content in mischmetall alloy

questiontext.text: Mischmetall is an important pyrophoric alloy consisting typically of approximately \(95\%\) lanthanoid metals, \(5\%\) iron, and trace impurities. What is the mass of lanthanoid metals contained in a \(250.0\text{ g}\) sample of standard mischmetall?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Total mass of mischmetall sample = \(250.0\text{ g}\). Mass percentage of lanthanoid metals = \(95\%\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The mass fraction is assumed uniform throughout the homogeneous alloy sample.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Mass of component is given by: \[\text{Mass} = \text{Total mass} \times \frac{\text{Percentage}}{100}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substituting the values: \[\text{Mass of lanthanoids} = 250.0\text{ g} \times \frac{95}{100} = 250.0\text{ g} \times 0.95 = 237.5\text{ g}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The calculated mass of \(237.5\text{ g}\) plus the iron mass of \(12.5\text{ g}\) equals \(250.0\text{ g}\), confirming the result.

Therefore, the correct answer is: \(237.5\text{ g}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_NUMERICAL_Q04 - Moles of iron(II) oxidised per mole of potassium permanganate in acid

questiontext.text: In acidic solution, potassium permanganate acts as a strong oxidising agent: \(\text{MnO}_4^- + 8\text{H}^+ + 5\text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{2+} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}\). How many moles of \(\text{Fe}^{2+}\) ions are completely oxidised to \(\text{Fe}^{3+}\) by \(1.0\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{KMnO}_4\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Amount of \(\text{KMnO}_4\) = \(1.0\text{ mol}\). The oxidation reaction converts \(\text{Fe}^{2+}\) to \(\text{Fe}^{3+}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The reaction is carried out in acidic medium where permanganate is reduced to manganese(II).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The half-reactions are: \[\text{MnO}_4^- + 8\text{H}^+ + 5\text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{2+} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}\] \[\text{Fe}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{Fe}^{3+} + \text{e}^-\] The balanced overall ionic redox equation is: \[\text{MnO}_4^- + 5\text{Fe}^{2+} + 8\text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{2+} + 5\text{Fe}^{3+} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
From the stoichiometric coefficients of the balanced equation, \(1\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{MnO}_4^-\) reacts with \(5\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{Fe}^{2+}\). Therefore, \(1.0\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{KMnO}_4\) oxidises exactly \(5.0\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{Fe}^{2+}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Electron balance: \(1\text{ mol} \times 5\text{ e}^- = 5\text{ mol} \times 1\text{ e}^- = 5\text{ mol e}^-\). The answer is \(5.0\text{ mol}\).

Therefore, the correct answer is: \(5.0\text{ mol}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_NUMERICAL_Q05 - Spin-only magnetic moment of chromium(II) cation

questiontext.text: What is the calculated 'spin-only' magnetic moment of the divalent chromium ion, \(\text{Cr}^{2+}\) (atomic number \(Z = 24\)), in units of Bohr Magnetons (BM)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The ion is \(\text{Cr}^{2+}\) with atomic number \(Z = 24\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The ground state configuration of neutral chromium is \([\text{Ar}]\,3d^54s^1\). Formation of \(\text{Cr}^{2+}\) entails loss of the single \(4s\) electron and one \(3d\) electron, giving \([\text{Ar}]\,3d^4\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The spin-only formula is \(\mu = \sqrt{n(n + 2)}\text{ BM}\), where \(n\) is the number of unpaired electrons.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
In the \(3d^4\) subshell, all four electrons remain unpaired in separate degenerate orbitals, so \(n = 4\). Substituting into the formula: \[\mu = \sqrt{4(4 + 2)} = \sqrt{24} \approx 4.90\text{ BM}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Four unpaired electrons give \(\sqrt{24} \approx 4.90\text{ BM}\), which matches Table 4.7.

Therefore, the correct answer is: \(4.90\text{ BM}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_NUMERICAL_Q06 - Magnetic moment of cerium(III) tripositive lanthanoid ion

questiontext.text: Using Hund's rule, determine the electronic configuration of the tripositive cerium ion, \(\text{Ce}^{3+}\) (atomic number \(Z = 58\)), and calculate its magnetic moment based on the 'spin-only' formula.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The element is cerium with atomic number \(Z = 58\). The ion is tripositive (\(\text{Ce}^{3+}\)).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The outer ground-state electronic configuration of neutral \(\text{Ce}\) is \([\text{Xe}]\,4f^15d^16s^2\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Formation of the tripositive cation \(\text{Ce}^{3+}\) involves loss of two \(6s\) electrons and one \(5d\) electron, yielding the configuration \([\text{Xe}]\,4f^1\). The spin-only magnetic moment formula is \(\mu = \sqrt{n(n + 2)}\text{ BM}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
The \(4f^1\) configuration contains exactly \(n = 1\) unpaired electron. Substituting \(n = 1\): \[\mu = \sqrt{1(1 + 2)} = \sqrt{3} \approx 1.73\text{ BM}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
One unpaired electron gives \(\sqrt{3} \approx 1.73\text{ BM}\), in complete agreement with theory.

Therefore, the correct answer is: \(1.73\text{ BM}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_NUMERICAL_Q07 - Difference in parallel spin exchange pairs between d5 and d4 configurations

questiontext.text: Exchange energy is proportional to the total number of possible pairs of parallel spins in degenerate orbitals: \(K = \frac{n(n - 1)}{2}\). What is the difference in the number of parallel spin exchange pairs between a half-filled \(3d^5\) ion (such as \(\text{Mn}^{2+}\)) and a \(3d^4\) ion (such as \(\text{Cr}^{2+}\))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Two electronic configurations are considered: \(3d^5\) (five parallel spins) and \(3d^4\) (four parallel spins) in five degenerate \(d\) orbitals.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
In both high-spin ions, all electrons occupy separate degenerate orbitals with parallel spins according to Hund's rule.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The number of possible exchange pairs among \(n\) electrons of parallel spin is given by the combination formula: \[K = \frac{n(n - 1)}{2}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
For \(3d^5\) (\(n = 5\)): \[K(3d^5) = \frac{5(5 - 1)}{2} = \frac{20}{2} = 10\text{ pairs}\] For \(3d^4\) (\(n = 4\)): \[K(3d^4) = \frac{4(4 - 1)}{2} = \frac{12}{2} = 6\text{ pairs}\] Difference in exchange pairs: \[\Delta K = 10 - 6 = 4\text{ pairs}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The loss of exchange energy corresponds to \(4\) exchange interactions, confirming the calculation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: \(4\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_NUMERICAL_Q08 - Moles of iodine liberated in copper(II) reaction with iodide

questiontext.text: When copper(II) ions are treated with excess potassium iodide in aqueous solution, copper(I) iodide precipitates and iodine is liberated: \(2\text{Cu}^{2+} + 4\text{I}^- \rightarrow \text{Cu}_2\text{I}_2\text{(s)} + \text{I}_2\). How many moles of \(\text{I}_2\) are formed when \(0.80\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{Cu}^{2+}\) reacts completely with excess iodide?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Amount of \(\text{Cu}^{2+}\) = \(0.80\text{ mol}\). Iodide ions are present in excess.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The reaction proceeds to completion according to the given stoichiometry with quantitative precipitation of copper(I) iodide.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The balanced chemical equation is: \[2\text{Cu}^{2+} + 4\text{I}^- \rightarrow \text{Cu}_2\text{I}_2\text{(s)} + \text{I}_2\] The stoichiometric molar ratio between \(\text{I}_2\) and \(\text{Cu}^{2+}\) is \(\frac{1\text{ mol }\text{I}_2}{2\text{ mol }\text{Cu}^{2+}}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Using the stoichiometric ratio: \[\text{Moles of }\text{I}_2 = 0.80\text{ mol }\text{Cu}^{2+} \times \frac{1\text{ mol }\text{I}_2}{2\text{ mol }\text{Cu}^{2+}} = 0.40\text{ mol}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
\(0.80\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{Cu}^{2+}\) accepts \(0.80\text{ mol}\) of electrons; \(0.40\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{I}_2\) is produced by releasing \(2 \times 0.40 = 0.80\text{ mol}\) of electrons. Charge and mass balance are preserved.

Therefore, the correct answer is: \(0.40\text{ mol}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_NUMERICAL_Q09 - Moles of tin(II) oxidised by acidified potassium dichromate

questiontext.text: In acidic solution, potassium dichromate oxidises tin(II) to tin(IV) according to the balanced equation: \(\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 14\text{H}^+ + 3\text{Sn}^{2+} \rightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 3\text{Sn}^{4+} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O}\). How many moles of \(\text{Sn}^{2+}\) can be completely oxidised by \(0.60\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Amount of \(\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7\) (\(\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}\)) = \(0.60\text{ mol}\). The solution is acidified with sufficient \(\text{H}^+\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Dichromate is reduced quantitatively to chromium(III) while tin(II) is oxidised to tin(IV).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
From the balanced equation: \[\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 14\text{H}^+ + 3\text{Sn}^{2+} \rightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 3\text{Sn}^{4+} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O}\] Each mole of \(\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}\) oxidises \(3\) moles of \(\text{Sn}^{2+}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculating moles of \(\text{Sn}^{2+}\): \[\text{Moles of }\text{Sn}^{2+} = 0.60\text{ mol }\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} \times \frac{3\text{ mol }\text{Sn}^{2+}}{1\text{ mol }\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}} = 1.80\text{ mol}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Total electron gain = \(0.60\text{ mol} \times 6 = 3.60\text{ mol e}^-\). Total electron loss = \(1.80\text{ mol} \times 2 = 3.60\text{ mol e}^-\). The answer is \(1.80\text{ mol}\).

Therefore, the correct answer is: \(1.80\text{ mol}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_NUMERICAL_Q10 - Moles of permanganate required to oxidise oxalate in acid

questiontext.text: Acidified potassium permanganate oxidises oxalate ions (\(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}\)) at \(333\text{ K}\) according to the balanced reaction: \(2\text{MnO}_4^- + 5\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} + 16\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 2\text{Mn}^{2+} + 8\text{H}_2\text{O} + 10\text{CO}_2\). How many moles of \(\text{KMnO}_4\) are required to react completely with \(2.50\text{ mol}\) of oxalate ions?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Amount of oxalate ions (\(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}\)) = \(2.50\text{ mol}\). The reaction occurs in warm acidic medium.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Oxalate is quantitatively oxidised to carbon dioxide gas while permanganate is reduced to manganese(II).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
According to the balanced ionic equation: \[2\text{MnO}_4^- + 5\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} + 16\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 2\text{Mn}^{2+} + 8\text{H}_2\text{O} + 10\text{CO}_2\] The stoichiometric mole ratio is: \[\frac{n(\text{MnO}_4^-)}{n(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-})} = \frac{2}{5}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substituting the given amount of oxalate: \[n(\text{MnO}_4^-) = 2.50\text{ mol} \times \frac{2}{5} = \frac{5.00}{5} = 1.00\text{ mol}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Electron check: \(1.00\text{ mol }\text{MnO}_4^- \times 5\text{ e}^- = 5.0\text{ mol e}^-\). \(2.50\text{ mol oxalate} \times 2\text{ e}^- = 5.0\text{ mol e}^-\). The answer is \(1.00\text{ mol}\).\n

Therefore, the correct answer is: \(1.00\text{ mol}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_NUMERICAL_Q11 - Volume of oxygen gas from thermal decomposition of potassium permanganate

questiontext.text: When solid potassium permanganate is heated to \(513\text{ K}\), it decomposes according to the reaction: \(2\text{KMnO}_4\text{(s)} \rightarrow \text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4\text{(s)} + \text{MnO}_2\text{(s)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)}\). What volume of \(\text{O}_2\) gas at standard temperature and pressure (STP, standard molar volume \(= 22.7\text{ L mol}^{-1}\)) is liberated upon complete thermal decomposition of \(0.40\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{KMnO}_4\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Amount of \(\text{KMnO}_4\) = \(0.40\text{ mol}\). Standard molar volume of ideal gas at STP (\(1\text{ bar}\), \(273.15\text{ K}\)) = \(22.7\text{ L mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The decomposition proceeds to completion according to the stoichiometric equation, and \(\text{O}_2\) behaves as an ideal gas.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
From the reaction: \[2\text{KMnO}_4 \rightarrow \text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4 + \text{MnO}_2 + \text{O}_2\] The mole ratio of \(\text{O}_2\) to \(\text{KMnO}_4\) is \(\frac{1}{2}\). Volume of gas at STP is \(V = n \times V_{\text{m}}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate moles of \(\text{O}_2\) produced: \[n(\text{O}_2) = 0.40\text{ mol }\text{KMnO}_4 \times \frac{1\text{ mol }\text{O}_2}{2\text{ mol }\text{KMnO}_4} = 0.20\text{ mol}\] Calculate volume of \(\text{O}_2\) at STP: \[V(\text{O}_2) = 0.20\text{ mol} \times 22.7\text{ L mol}^{-1} = 4.54\text{ L}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Units are litres (\(\text{L}\)). Moles: \(0.20\text{ mol}\); volume: \(0.20 \times 22.7 = 4.54\text{ L}\).

Therefore, the correct answer is: \(4.54\text{ L}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_NUMERICAL_Q12 - Moles of permanganate produced from disproportionation of manganate

questiontext.text: In acidic or neutral aqueous solution, dark green manganate(VI) ions undergo disproportionation: \(3\text{MnO}_4^{2-} + 4\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 2\text{MnO}_4^- + \text{MnO}_2\text{(s)} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}\). How many moles of purple permanganate ions (\(\text{MnO}_4^-\)) are formed when \(1.50\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{MnO}_4^{2-}\) completely disproportionates?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Amount of manganate(VI) ions (\(\text{MnO}_4^{2-}\)) = \(1.50\text{ mol}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Manganese(VI) undergoes complete disproportionation into manganese(VII) and manganese(IV).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The stoichiometric equation is: \[3\text{MnO}_4^{2-} + 4\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 2\text{MnO}_4^- + \text{MnO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}\] The stoichiometric ratio is \(\frac{2\text{ mol }\text{MnO}_4^-}{3\text{ mol }\text{MnO}_4^{2-}}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculating moles of \(\text{MnO}_4^-\): \[n(\text{MnO}_4^-) = 1.50\text{ mol }\text{MnO}_4^{2-} \times \frac{2\text{ mol }\text{MnO}_4^-}{3\text{ mol }\text{MnO}_4^{2-}} = 1.00\text{ mol}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
From \(1.50\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{Mn}^{\text{VI}}\), \(1.00\text{ mol}\) oxidises to \(\text{Mn}^{\text{VII}}\) (losing \(1.00\text{ mol e}^-\)) and \(0.50\text{ mol}\) reduces to \(\text{Mn}^{\text{IV}}\) (gaining \(0.50 \times 2 = 1.00\text{ mol e}^-\)). The redox balance is verified.

Therefore, the correct answer is: \(1.00\text{ mol}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_NUMERICAL_Q13 - Occupancy of t2g orbitals in hydrated nickel(II) octahedral complex

questiontext.text: In an octahedral aqueous coordination complex of nickel(II), \([\text{Ni}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}\), how many electrons occupy the lower-energy \(t_{2\text{g}}\) set of \(d\) orbitals?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The central cation is \(\text{Ni}^{2+}\) in an octahedral ligand field surrounded by six neutral \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\) ligands. Atomic number of nickel is \(Z = 28\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Neutral nickel has ground-state configuration \([\text{Ar}]\,3d^84s^2\). Formation of \(\text{Ni}^{2+}\) yields \([\text{Ar}]\,3d^8\). In an octahedral crystal field, the five \(d\) orbitals split into a triply degenerate lower \(t_{2\text{g}}\) set and a doubly degenerate higher \(e_{\text{g}}\) set.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
According to Hund's rule and Aufbau principle in weak-field/standard octahedral complexes: electrons fill \(t_{2\text{g}}\) singly, then \(e_{\text{g}}\) singly, then pair in \(t_{2\text{g}}\), followed by \(e_{\text{g}}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
For \(8\) electrons in an octahedral field: First \(3\) electrons enter \(t_{2\text{g}}\) (\(t_{2\text{g}}^3\)). Next \(2\) electrons enter \(e_{\text{g}}\) (\(e_{\text{g}}^2\)). The remaining \(3\) electrons pair up in the \(t_{2\text{g}}\) orbitals, giving: \[t_{2\text{g}}^6 e_{\text{g}}^2\] Therefore, the number of electrons occupying the \(t_{2\text{g}}\) set is \(6\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Total electrons: \(6 + 2 = 8\). The number of electrons in the \(t_{2\text{g}}\) orbitals is \(6\).

Therefore, the correct answer is: \(6\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_NUMERICAL_Q14 - Moles of sulphur precipitated from hydrogen sulphide by dichromate

questiontext.text: Acidified potassium dichromate oxidises hydrogen sulphide gas, precipitating elemental sulphur according to the reaction: \(\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 8\text{H}^+ + 3\text{H}_2\text{S} \rightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 3\text{S}\text{(s)} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O}\). How many moles of sulphur are precipitated when \(0.40\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7\) reacts with excess \(\text{H}_2\text{S}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Amount of \(\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7\) = \(0.40\text{ mol}\). Hydrogen sulphide gas (\(\text{H}_2\text{S}\)) is present in excess in acidic solution.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The reaction proceeds quantitatively according to the stoichiometric redox equation.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The balanced chemical equation is: \[\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 8\text{H}^+ + 3\text{H}_2\text{S} \rightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 3\text{S} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O}\] Each mole of \(\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}\) produces \(3\) moles of solid sulphur.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Using the stoichiometric relationship: \[n(\text{S}) = 0.40\text{ mol }\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} \times \frac{3\text{ mol S}}{1\text{ mol }\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}} = 1.20\text{ mol}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
\(0.40\text{ mol}\) of dichromate accepts \(0.40 \times 6 = 2.40\text{ mol e}^-\). Each sulphide loses \(2\text{ e}^-\), so \(1.20\text{ mol} \times 2 = 2.40\text{ mol e}^-\). The answer is \(1.20\text{ mol}\).

Therefore, the correct answer is: \(1.20\text{ mol}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_NUMERICAL_Q15 - Net enthalpy change for transformation of solid copper to aqueous ion

questiontext.text: Using the thermochemical data from Table 4.4 for the transformation \(\text{Cu(s)} \rightarrow \text{Cu}^{2+}\text{(aq)} + 2\text{e}^-\): enthalpy of atomisation \(\Delta_{\text{a}}H^\circ = +339\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\), first ionisation enthalpy \(\Delta_{\text{i}}H_1^\circ = +745\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\), second ionisation enthalpy \(\Delta_{\text{i}}H_2^\circ = +1958\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\), and hydration enthalpy \(\Delta_{\text{hyd}}H^\circ(\text{Cu}^{2+}) = -2121\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\), calculate the net standard enthalpy change for this transformation.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
\(\Delta_{\text{a}}H^\circ = +339\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\), \(\Delta_{\text{i}}H_1^\circ = +745\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\), \(\Delta_{\text{i}}H_2^\circ = +1958\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\), \(\Delta_{\text{hyd}}H^\circ = -2121\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The Born-Haber thermochemical cycle applies Hess's law to sum the atomisation, ionisation, and hydration enthalpy terms.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The net enthalpy change \(\Delta_{\text{total}}H^\circ\) is: \[\Delta_{\text{total}}H^\circ = \Delta_{\text{a}}H^\circ + \Delta_{\text{i}}H_1^\circ + \Delta_{\text{i}}H_2^\circ + \Delta_{\text{hyd}}H^\circ\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substituting the numerical values line by line: \[\Delta_{\text{total}}H^\circ = 339 + 745 + 1958 + (-2121)\] Sum of atomisation and ionisation terms: \[339 + 745 + 1958 = +3042\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\] Adding the negative hydration enthalpy: \[\Delta_{\text{total}}H^\circ = 3042 - 2121 = +921\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The positive value of \(+921\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\) indicates an endothermic process, explaining why copper has a positive standard reduction potential and does not liberate \(\text{H}_2\) from dilute acids.

Therefore, the correct answer is: \(+921\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_NUMERICAL_Q16 - Net enthalpy change for transformation of solid zinc to aqueous ion

questiontext.text: From the thermochemical parameters in Table 4.4: for metallic zinc, enthalpy of atomisation \(\Delta_{\text{a}}H^\circ = +130\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\), first ionisation enthalpy \(\Delta_{\text{i}}H_1^\circ = +906\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\), second ionisation enthalpy \(\Delta_{\text{i}}H_2^\circ = +1734\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\), and hydration enthalpy \(\Delta_{\text{hyd}}H^\circ(\text{Zn}^{2+}) = -2059\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\). Calculate the net enthalpy change for the transformation \(\text{Zn(s)} \rightarrow \text{Zn}^{2+}\text{(aq)} + 2\text{e}^-\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
\(\Delta_{\text{a}}H^\circ = +130\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\), \(\Delta_{\text{i}}H_1^\circ = +906\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\), \(\Delta_{\text{i}}H_2^\circ = +1734\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\), \(\Delta_{\text{hyd}}H^\circ = -2059\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Standard thermodynamic cycle conditions apply; endothermic inputs are positive and exothermic hydration is negative.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
By Hess's law: \[\Delta_{\text{total}}H^\circ = \Delta_{\text{a}}H^\circ + \Delta_{\text{i}}H_1^\circ + \Delta_{\text{i}}H_2^\circ + \Delta_{\text{hyd}}H^\circ\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Sum the atomisation and ionisation enthalpies: \[130 + 906 + 1734 = +2770\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\] Add the negative hydration enthalpy: \[\Delta_{\text{total}}H^\circ = 2770 - 2059 = +711\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Units are \(\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\). The sum is \(+711\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\), significantly lower than copper's \(+921\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\), consistent with zinc's negative reduction potential (\(-0.76\text{ V}\)).

Therefore, the correct answer is: \(+711\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_NUMERICAL_Q17 - Moles of electrons transferred per mole of thiosulphate oxidised by alkaline permanganate

questiontext.text: In neutral or faintly alkaline solution, permanganate oxidises thiosulphate almost quantitatively to sulphate according to the reaction: \(8\text{MnO}_4^- + 3\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 8\text{MnO}_2 + 6\text{SO}_4^{2-} + 2\text{OH}^-\). How many moles of electrons are transferred per mole of thiosulphate (\(\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}\)) oxidised?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The reaction is: \(8\text{MnO}_4^- + 3\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 8\text{MnO}_2 + 6\text{SO}_4^{2-} + 2\text{OH}^-\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Oxidation numbers: In \(\text{MnO}_4^-\), manganese is in the \(+7\) state; in \(\text{MnO}_2\), manganese is in the \(+4\) state. In \(\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}\), average oxidation state of sulphur is \(+2\); in \(\text{SO}_4^{2-}\), sulphur is in the \(+6\) state.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Total electrons gained by permanganate equals total electrons lost by thiosulphate. Electron loss per mole of \(\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}\) is: \[n(\text{e}^-) = 2 \times (\text{O.S.}_{\text{final}} - \text{O.S.}_{\text{initial}})\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Each manganese atom is reduced from \(+7\) to \(+4\), gaining \(3\text{ e}^-\). For \(8\) moles of \(\text{MnO}_4^-\), total electrons gained: \[8 \times 3 = 24\text{ mol of electrons}\] These \(24\text{ mol of electrons}\) are supplied by \(3\text{ mol of }\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}\). Therefore, electrons transferred per mole of \(\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}\): \[\frac{24\text{ mol e}^-}{3\text{ mol }\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}} = 8\text{ mol e}^-\] Alternatively, for each sulphur atom: \(+2 \rightarrow +6\) corresponds to a change of \(4\text{ e}^-\). Since there are two sulphur atoms per thiosulphate ion, \(2 \times 4 = 8\text{ mol e}^-\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Both the reduction half-reaction calculation and the oxidation half-reaction calculation yield \(8\text{ mol}\) of electrons per mole of thiosulphate.

Therefore, the correct answer is: \(8\text{ mol}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_NUMERICAL_Q18 - Moles of permanganate required to oxidise iodide to iodate in alkaline solution

questiontext.text: In neutral or faintly alkaline solution, potassium permanganate oxidises iodide ions to iodate ions: \(2\text{MnO}_4^- + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{I}^- \rightarrow 2\text{MnO}_2 + 2\text{OH}^- + \text{IO}_3^-\). What is the minimum amount of \(\text{KMnO}_4\) (in moles) required to completely oxidise \(0.35\text{ mol}\) of potassium iodide (\(\text{KI}\)) to potassium iodate?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Amount of iodide (\(\text{I}^-\)) = \(0.35\text{ mol}\). Medium is neutral or faintly alkaline.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Iodide is oxidised exclusively to iodate (\(\text{IO}_3^-\)), and permanganate is reduced to manganese dioxide (\(\text{MnO}_2\)).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
From the balanced chemical equation: \[2\text{MnO}_4^- + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{I}^- \rightarrow 2\text{MnO}_2 + 2\text{OH}^- + \text{IO}_3^-\] The stoichiometric mole ratio is: \[\frac{n(\text{MnO}_4^-)}{n(\text{I}^-)} = \frac{2}{1}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the required moles of \(\text{KMnO}_4\): \[n(\text{KMnO}_4) = 0.35\text{ mol }\text{I}^- \times \frac{2\text{ mol }\text{MnO}_4^-}{1\text{ mol }\text{I}^-} = 0.70\text{ mol}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Electron check: Oxidation of \(\text{I}^-\) (\(-1\)) to \(\text{IO}_3^-\) (\(+5\)) releases \(6\text{ e}^-\). For \(0.35\text{ mol}\), total electrons \(= 0.35 \times 6 = 2.10\text{ mol e}^-\). Reduction of \(\text{Mn}^{\text{VII}}\) to \(\text{Mn}^{\text{IV}}\) requires \(3\text{ e}^-\). Total \(\text{KMnO}_4 = \frac{2.10}{3} = 0.70\text{ mol}\). Calculation is verified.

Therefore, the correct answer is: \(0.70\text{ mol}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_NUMERICAL_Q19 - Mass percentage of chromium in pure chromite ore

questiontext.text: Potassium dichromate is industrially manufactured from chromite ore, which has the chemical formula \(\text{FeCr}_2\text{O}_4\). Given the molar atomic masses: \(\text{Fe} = 56.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), \(\text{Cr} = 52.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), and \(\text{O} = 16.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), calculate the percentage by mass of chromium in pure chromite ore.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Formula of chromite: \(\text{FeCr}_2\text{O}_4\). Atomic masses: \(\text{Fe} = 56.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), \(\text{Cr} = 52.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), \(\text{O} = 16.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The sample is assumed to be chemically pure iron(II) chromite.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Molar mass of compound is: \[M = M(\text{Fe}) + 2 \times M(\text{Cr}) + 4 \times M(\text{O})\] Mass percentage of chromium is: \[\%\text{ Cr} = \frac{2 \times M(\text{Cr})}{M(\text{FeCr}_2\text{O}_4)} \times 100\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the molar mass of \(\text{FeCr}_2\text{O}_4\): \[M = 56.0 + 2(52.0) + 4(16.0) = 56.0 + 104.0 + 64.0 = 224.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}\] Total mass of chromium in one mole: \[m(\text{Cr}) = 2 \times 52.0 = 104.0\text{ g}\] Calculate percentage by mass: \[\%\text{ Cr} = \frac{104.0}{224.0} \times 100 = \frac{13}{28} \times 100 \approx 46.43\%\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Units are percent (\(\%\)). Mass percentages: \(\text{Fe} = \frac{56}{224} = 25\%\), \(\text{O} = \frac{64}{224} \approx 28.57\%\), \(\text{Cr} = 46.43\%\). Total \(= 25 + 28.57 + 46.43 = 100.0\%\).

Therefore, the correct answer is: \(46.43\%\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_NUMERICAL_Q20 - Titration volume calculation of potassium permanganate solution for iron(II)

questiontext.text: A \(25.0\text{ mL}\) sample of an acidified aqueous solution containing \(\text{Fe}^{2+}\) ions at a concentration of \(0.080\text{ M}\) is titrated against standard \(0.020\text{ M}\) potassium permanganate (\(\text{KMnO}_4\)) solution. What volume of the \(\text{KMnO}_4\) solution is required to reach the equivalence point?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Volume of \(\text{Fe}^{2+}\) solution \(V_1 = 25.0\text{ mL}\). Molarity of \(\text{Fe}^{2+}\) solution \(M_1 = 0.080\text{ M}\). Molarity of \(\text{KMnO}_4\) solution \(M_2 = 0.020\text{ M}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Titration occurs in acidic solution where \(\text{MnO}_4^-\) is reduced to \(\text{Mn}^{2+}\) and \(\text{Fe}^{2+}\) is oxidised to \(\text{Fe}^{3+}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The balanced redox equation is: \[\text{MnO}_4^- + 5\text{Fe}^{2+} + 8\text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{2+} + 5\text{Fe}^{3+} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}\] At equivalence point: \[n(\text{MnO}_4^-) = \frac{1}{5} n(\text{Fe}^{2+}) \implies M_2 V_2 = \frac{1}{5} M_1 V_1\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate millimoles of \(\text{Fe}^{2+}\): \[\text{mmol of }\text{Fe}^{2+} = 25.0\text{ mL} \times 0.080\text{ M} = 2.00\text{ mmol}\] Calculate required millimoles of \(\text{MnO}_4^-\): \[\text{mmol of }\text{MnO}_4^- = \frac{2.00\text{ mmol}}{5} = 0.40\text{ mmol}\] Calculate volume of \(0.020\text{ M}\) \(\text{KMnO}_4\): \[V_2 = \frac{\text{mmol of }\text{MnO}_4^-}{M_2} = \frac{0.40\text{ mmol}}{0.020\text{ mmol mL}^{-1}} = 20.0\text{ mL}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Check: \(20.0\text{ mL} \times 0.020\text{ M} \times 5 = 2.00\text{ mmol}\), which equals \(25.0\text{ mL} \times 0.080\text{ M} \times 1 = 2.00\text{ mmol}\). The equivalence volume is \(20.0\text{ mL}\).

Therefore, the correct answer is: \(20.0\text{ mL}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_SEQUENCING_Q01 - Preparation steps of potassium dichromate from ore

questiontext.text:
Potassium dichromate (\(\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7\)) is manufactured industrially from chromite ore (\(\text{FeCr}_2\text{O}_4\)). Arrange the following operational steps in the correct chronological sequence:

  1. Fusion of chromite ore with sodium carbonate in free access of air to produce sodium chromate.
  2. Extraction of the fused mass with water and filtration to separate insoluble iron(III) oxide from yellow sodium chromate solution.
  3. Acidification of the yellow sodium chromate solution with sulphuric acid to obtain orange sodium dichromate.
  4. Treatment of the sodium dichromate solution with potassium chloride to crystallise potassium dichromate.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The industrial synthesis of potassium dichromate utilizes chromite ore (\(\text{FeCr}_2\text{O}_4\)) as the starting raw material, proceeding via initial conversion to soluble sodium chromate, subsequent conversion to sodium dichromate by acid, and finally metathesis to less soluble potassium dichromate.

Step 2: Alkaline Oxidative Fusion
Finely powdered chromite ore is fused with sodium carbonate (\(\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\)) in a reverberatory furnace in excess air to oxidize chromium from +3 to +6:
\[4\text{FeCr}_2\text{O}_4 + 8\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 + 7\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 8\text{Na}_2\text{CrO}_4 + 2\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3 + 8\text{CO}_2\]

Step 3: Extraction and Filtration
The roasted mass is extracted with water. Sodium chromate dissolves completely to give a yellow solution, while iron(III) oxide remains as an insoluble residue and is filtered off.

Step 4: Acidification to Dichromate
The yellow sodium chromate filtrate is acidified with concentrated sulphuric acid, converting chromate into orange sodium dichromate:
\[2\text{Na}_2\text{CrO}_4 + 2\text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 + 2\text{Na}^+ + \text{H}_2\text{O}\]

Step 5: Metathesis with Potassium Chloride and Final Answer
Because sodium dichromate is highly soluble and deliquescent, it is treated with potassium chloride. Potassium dichromate is much less soluble in cold water and precipitates out as orange crystals:
\[\text{Na}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 + 2\text{KCl} \rightarrow \text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 + 2\text{NaCl}\]
Therefore, the correct chronological sequence is oxidative fusion of chromite ore with sodium carbonate, followed by extraction and filtration, followed by acidification to produce sodium dichromate, and concluded by treatment with potassium chloride to crystallise potassium dichromate (\(\text{I} \rightarrow \text{II} \rightarrow \text{III} \rightarrow \text{IV}\)).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_SEQUENCING_Q02 - Thermodynamic stages of metal cation hydration process

questiontext.text:
The thermochemical transformation of a transition metal from its standard solid state, \(\text{M(s)}\), to its hydrated divalent cation, \(\text{M}^{2+}\text{(aq)}\), is governed by a Born-Haber energy cycle. Arrange the energetic stages of this process in the correct logical sequence:

  1. Sublimation/atomisation of the solid metal into individual gaseous atoms: \(\text{M(s)} \rightarrow \text{M(g)}\)
  2. First ionisation of the gaseous metal atom to produce a gaseous unipositive cation: \(\text{M(g)} \rightarrow \text{M}^+\text{(g)} + \text{e}^-\)
  3. Second ionisation of the unipositive cation to produce a gaseous dipositive cation: \(\text{M}^+\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{M}^{2+}\text{(g)} + \text{e}^-\)
  4. Hydration of the dipositive gaseous cation by solvent water molecules: \(\text{M}^{2+}\text{(g)} + \text{aq} \rightarrow \text{M}^{2+}\text{(aq)}\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The standard reduction potential \(E^\circ(\text{M}^{2+}/\text{M})\) of a transition metal depends on the overall enthalpy change for transforming \(\text{M(s)}\) into \(\text{M}^{2+}\text{(aq)}\). In the thermochemical cycle, metallic bonds must first be broken, then electrons are removed sequentially, and finally the resulting gaseous cation interacts with water.

Step 2: Sublimation Stage
The solid metal crystal lattice must first absorb enthalpy of atomisation (\(\Delta_a H^\circ\)) to produce separated gaseous neutral atoms:
\[\text{M(s)} \rightarrow \text{M(g)}\]

Step 3: Successive Ionisation Stages
The isolated gaseous atom loses its outermost electrons one by one. The first ionisation requires the first ionisation enthalpy (\(\Delta_i H^\circ_1\)):
\[\text{M(g)} \rightarrow \text{M}^+\text{(g)} + \text{e}^-\]
Next, removal of the second electron requires the second ionisation enthalpy (\(\Delta_i H^\circ_2\)):
\[\text{M}^+\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{M}^{2+}\text{(g)} + \text{e}^-\]

Step 4: Hydration Stage and Final Answer
The gaseous divalent cation \(\text{M}^{2+}\text{(g)}\) is then solvated by water molecules, releasing hydration enthalpy (\(\Delta_{\text{hyd}} H^\circ\)):
\[\text{M}^{2+}\text{(g)} + \text{aq} \rightarrow \text{M}^{2+}\text{(aq)}\]
Hence, the correct logical progression of energetic stages is atomisation of solid metal, followed by first ionisation, second ionisation, and concluding with hydration of the gaseous divalent cation (\(\text{I} \rightarrow \text{II} \rightarrow \text{III} \rightarrow \text{IV}\)).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_THE_D_AND_F_BLOCK_ELEMENTS_SEQUENCING_Q03 - Commercial preparation steps of potassium permanganate

questiontext.text:
Commercial manufacturing of potassium permanganate (\(\text{KMnO}_4\)) from pyrolusite ore (\(\text{MnO}_2\)) involves alkaline oxidative fusion followed by electrochemical oxidation. Arrange the following industrial steps in the correct chronological sequence:

  1. Alkaline oxidative fusion of pyrolusite ore (\(\text{MnO}_2\)) with molten potassium hydroxide in the presence of air or \(\text{KNO}_3\).
  2. Dissolution and extraction of the fused mass to obtain an alkaline dark green solution of potassium manganate (\(\text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4\)).
  3. Electrolytic oxidation of the green manganate(VI) solution at the anode to form purple permanganate(VII).
